newsitem.title: UK: Finer wool tops savaged by sterling in Bradford.
newsitem.headline: Finer wool tops savaged by sterling in Bradford.

text.p: Sterling's recovery against a strengthening U.S. dollar hacked up to thirteen pence per kilo off fine tops prices, abetted by easing raw merino values in Australia and South Africa, market sources said on Thursday.
One analyst said traders were non-commital, unwilling to predict which way the market would move after a fortnight of significant volatility in the world's primary markets.
Some traders saw last week's low stockpile disposals in Australia as a sign of limited demand and reported a total lack of interest in Bradford tops.
Others said local increases in the price of noils (the short-fibres removed in the combing process) reflected steady demand from wool users.
But reports of genuine buying interest were few and far between and one industry commentator said the bullish view was borne out by local corporate results.
Finest 70s Super experienced the biggest price fall (thirteen percent) while 64s Super and Blended both lost seven pence per kg.
Tops of purely English origin held their values steady at 258-271 pence per kg. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
